article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: Face Mints × Biscotti × Sherb BX
Breeder: Seed Junky Genetics
THC Content: 24–30%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: limonene , myrcene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Diesel, sour citrus, mint, vanilla
Flowering Time (Indoor): 65–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Gas Face does not hide what kind of cannabis it wants to be. The aroma hits with the sharpness of fresh fuel before sour lime, mint, vanilla, damp earth, and sweet pastry begin separating from the background. Dense flowers can appear almost armored in resin, carrying the chunky structure associated with modern Kush and Cookies breeding while retaining a pungency that points much further back toward OG.

Seed Junky Genetics built the cultivar from Face Mints and a Biscotti × Sherb backcross, creating marijuana that brings old-school gas into the dessert era without allowing sweetness to tame the fuel. High THC is common, but raw potency is only part of the appeal. The experience often begins with an unusually clear, elevated headspace before accumulating enough physical weight to turn an active evening into something considerably slower.
Genetics and Lineage

Seed Junky Genetics created Gas Face by crossing Face Mints with Biscotti × Sherb BX. The pedigree is preserved by growers working with the original genetics, including the Cannabis Horticultural Association, which identifies its Gas Face breeding material as Face Mints × (Biscotti × Sherb BX). Commercial cultivator Good Chemistry independently maintains the same lineage.

Face Mints supplies much of the cultivar’s OG-driven personality. Its lineage combines Face Off OG with Kush Mints , bringing sharp Kush fuel, mint, resin production, and substantial potency into the cross. The other side folds Biscotti into a Sherbet backcross, contributing vanilla, baked sweetness, cream, citrus, and the dense flower morphology associated with California dessert genetics. Put together, the family tree contains a striking amount of modern cannabis history: OG Kush influence from Face Off, Kush Mints potency, Biscotti’s Cookie-and-OG richness, and Sherbet’s fruit-and-cream character.

That pedigree is also why simplified descriptions such as Face Mints × Biscotti leave out an important part of the strain. Sherb BX is not a minor footnote; it helps explain the sweet citrus and creamy layer beneath the aggressive gas. Gas Face therefore belongs to the Seed Junky school of breeding where powerful OG-derived marijuana is reinforced with modern resin, flower density, and dessert terpenes rather than replaced by them.
Effects and Experience

The first few minutes can be surprisingly lucid. A strong cerebral lift may appear quickly, sharpening interest in music, conversation, movies, or whatever happens to be occupying attention. Mood tends to move upward before the body becomes especially heavy, giving moderate amounts a window in which the strain can feel creative and socially engaging rather than purely sedating.

That balance rarely remains unchanged. Physical relaxation accumulates gradually through the shoulders, torso, and legs, while the brighter mental high becomes deeper and less urgent. The effect can feel almost deceptive because mental clarity may persist while motivation steadily drops. Stronger sessions commonly end in a much heavier state, especially for consumers accustomed to taking large inhalations of potent weed.

Gas Face regularly appears in high-THC form. A Maine-grown Gas Face #10, for example, was documented above 25% THC, while other modern expressions approach or exceed 30%. Potency varies by phenotype and cultivation, so the number on a specific laboratory report is more useful than a universal average. High doses may cause dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, anxiety, impaired memory, or substantial sleepiness.
Medical Benefits

The shift from cerebral uplift into physical calm may appeal to medical marijuana consumers who prefer an experience that does not begin with immediate sedation. During the earlier portion, the elevated mood can make ordinary stress feel less demanding, while the later body effect may temporarily make muscular tension or general discomfort less prominent. Appetite can also become noticeably stronger as the experience deepens.

Those qualities help explain why some consumers choose high-THC indica hybrids when dealing with evening stress, appetite difficulties, physical discomfort, or trouble settling down at night. Gas Face itself, however, has not been clinically demonstrated to treat insomnia, anxiety, depression, chronic pain, or another particular condition. Cannabis strain names are not standardized medical formulations, and cannabinoid concentrations can differ substantially between producers.

For medical use, the analysis of the actual flower matters more than the strain reputation. A batch approaching 30% THC demands very different dosing than weaker marijuana, particularly for someone with limited tolerance. Patients taking prescription medication or managing significant health conditions should discuss cannabis use with a qualified healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fuel dominates the first encounter. The aroma can resemble gasoline, sour petroleum, rubber, and skunk before citrus starts to cut through the heavier notes. Lime peel and sour orange provide acidity, while mint adds a cooler edge inherited from Face Mints. Once the flower is ground, vanilla, cookie dough, leather, earth, and creamy Sherbet character can become considerably easier to detect.

The Cannabis Horticultural Association describes selected Gas Face plants as expressing berries, gas, petrol, floral aromatics, and powerful fuel. Other professionally grown versions emphasize diesel and skunk, demonstrating how phenotype and environment can shift individual details without erasing the central gassy identity.

Limonene, myrcene, and beta-caryophyllene commonly appear among prominent terpenes in tested commercial flower. Limonene aligns with the sharp citrus quality, caryophyllene contributes peppery depth, and myrcene can reinforce the earthy or musky foundation. These compounds should not be treated as a fixed breeder recipe; terpene proportions change with phenotype, environment, maturity, curing, and storage.
Growing Information

Gas Face generally develops the dense, resin-heavy flower structure expected from its ancestry. Plants can produce thick, closely packed buds with prominent trichome coverage and dark green coloration, sometimes accompanied by purple tones. Branching can support a broad indoor canopy, making topping, trellising, or other forms of canopy management useful where growers want to distribute light across more flowering sites.

Flowering estimates cluster around roughly 65–70 days, putting the cultivar close to nine or ten weeks indoors. Some preserved Seed Junky seed listings specify 68–70 days, while other cultivation references place the finish closer to 65 days. That difference is small enough to be explained by phenotype and harvest preference, so growers should judge maturity from the actual flowers rather than treating a specific calendar day as mandatory.

Reliable original yield figures are harder to establish, and exaggerated seed-retailer numbers should be treated cautiously. The strain is better documented for resin, density, and flower quality than for record-breaking production. Because mature buds can become compact and heavy, good airflow and humidity control are especially important during late bloom. Outdoors, the flowering duration generally places maturity during October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates, with dry autumn conditions preferable for protecting dense flowers.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Gas Face?

Gas Face was bred by Seed Junky Genetics from Face Mints × (Biscotti × Sherb BX). Face Mints itself carries Face Off OG and Kush Mints genetics, while the second parent brings Biscotti and Sherbet-family influences into the pedigree.
Is Gas Face indica or sativa?

It is generally considered an indica-dominant hybrid, commonly described around 70% indica and 30% sativa. The effects can initially feel more balanced because the cerebral uplift appears before deeper physical relaxation develops.
How strong is Gas Face weed?

Gas Face is a high-potency cannabis cultivar. Commercial flower commonly reaches the mid-to-upper 20% THC range, while exceptional expressions can test around 30% or higher. Actual potency should always be determined from the laboratory results of the specific product.
What does Gas Face taste like?

Diesel and sour fuel dominate, followed by citrus, lime, mint, vanilla, earth, skunk, and creamy cookie notes. Face Mints supplies much of the OG-and-mint character, while Biscotti and Sherb BX soften the profile with pastry and sweet citrus.
Did Gas Face win an Emerald Cup award?
Yes. Gas Face grown by Sense took second place in the Indoor Flower category at the 2023 Emerald Cup. The cultivar finished behind Fig Farms’ Blue Face and ahead of Cannabiotix’s French Alps.
Final Thoughts on Gas Face

Gas Face represents the modern return of fuel-forward cannabis without abandoning the advances of contemporary California breeding. Seed Junky combined the OG-heavy Face Mints line with Biscotti × Sherb BX, allowing petroleum, mint, citrus, earth, vanilla, and Cookie sweetness to occupy the same flower. That chemistry gives the strain substantially more depth than marijuana bred around sweetness alone.

Its reputation is also backed by more than THC percentages. Dense resinous buds, powerful aroma, a cerebral-to-physical effect progression, and a second-place finish in the 2023 Emerald Cup Indoor Flower competition have given the cultivar genuine staying power in a crowded market. For cannabis enthusiasts who prefer gas, Kush, Sour-style pungency, and heavy potency but still appreciate the creamier dimensions of modern dessert genetics, Gas Face is one of Seed Junky Genetics’ clearest expressions of both worlds.
